first.rationale: Activation messaging is the highest-probability sustainable play given current conditions. Memory 91 shows it improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action. With activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4%, internal engagement friction is the likely culprit—not pricing. Promotional pricing (memory 73) materially harmed retention and is inappropriate given our primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue. Referral incentives (memory 57) work well for established customers but don't address the immediate activation decline. Simplifying onboarding (memory 86) is proven, but activation_messaging directly targets the behavioral bottleneck we're seeing. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) is a different segment strategy. A standard_experiment on activation messaging inside the product can clarify whether messaging refinement can recover the 6% activation dip without the retention costs of discounting or the dependency on customer maturity (referrals). This preserves our optionality and avoids the well-documented downside risk of promotional pricing.

A standard_experiment on activation_messaging can credibly recover the activation decline while preserving retention gains and long-term revenue quality. This aligns with sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure is real, but memory_73 is explicit: promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized as growth strategy. Deploying it now would sacrifice long-term qualified revenue—our stated primary objective—for short-term churn stoppage. That is strategically misaligned. Activation_messaging remains the highest-conviction lever: exp_91 showed +6% activation and +1% retention with no downside. Recovering our 6% activation decline addresses an efficiency loss that compounds customer lifetime value. Price-sensitive churn is a segment issue, not a product-market fit issue. Activation_messaging can improve product stickiness and perceived value, indirectly reducing price sensitivity. This preserves margin and sustainability. However, I flag downstream_value_risk: if churn accelerates faster than activation_messaging can recover it, we may face a retention crisis. Leadership should be advised that promotional pricing offers faster tactical churn relief but at documented long-term cost, while activation_messaging is the sustainable play that requires holding the line on positioning. Standard_experiment scope allows rapid signal.
